headline: Office Manager Resigns After Finding 'Hidden Door' In New Building Leads Directly Into Opposing Political Party’s Breakroom
body:
The relocation process for a prominent administrative department turned into a minor diplomatic crisis this morning when the facilities manager discovered that the architectural plans for their new office had been accidentally inverted, creating a shared wall with the local headquarters of the opposition party. Employees attempting to enter the copier room have instead found themselves emerging directly into the rival group's mid-morning tea break.

“I walked in expecting to staple a few quarterly reports and was immediately handed a samosa and asked for my stance on the upcoming municipal tender process,” said Rajesh Sharma, a junior clerk who has now inadvertently joined three sub-committees of the rival faction. “The coffee is admittedly much better on their side of the wall, which I suppose is why the building committee chose this location in the first place.”

Opposition spokespeople have since issued a formal statement calling the proximity a ‘cynical attempt at intelligence gathering through the medium of catering,’ while the building management maintains the overlap was a purely logistical error caused by a misread blueprint. Contractors are currently attempting to install a heavy velvet curtain to maintain party decorum, though reports suggest employees from both sides have already begun swapping office chairs and printer toner.
caption: When the office floor plan is based on a game of Snakes and Ladders. #OfficeHumor #Politics #WorkLife #Relocation (satire)
igHook: Would you stay for the free samosas if your office accidentally merged with the competition?
